raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Enable dynamic EPLB on Ascend with `--enable-eplb`, using the existing planner and single-layer weight-migration algorithm. The integration supplies valid expert-route statistics and handles NPU weight formats while preserving the storage addresses used by captured graphs.

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| [`eplb/expert_distribution.py`](https://github.com/AkiYangDev/sglang/blob/9f037d735636e56efc2b2fb372900404bcbc3a25/python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_distribution.py) | Select the existing valid-TopK gatherer for NPU DeepEP; allocate utilization-broadcast tensors on the runtime device. |
| [`eplb/expert_location_updater.py`](https://github.com/AkiYangDev/sglang/blob/9f037d735636e56efc2b2fb372900404bcbc3a25/python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location_updater.py) | Dispatch NPU updates to the staging helper; keep the shared single-layer migration algorithm. |
| [`hardware_backend/npu/eplb.py`](https://github.com/AkiYangDev/sglang/blob/9f037d735636e56efc2b2fb372900404bcbc3a25/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/eplb.py) | Validate topology, select participating layers/ranks, stage ND weights, bound temporary allocations, and restore weights in place. |

## 1. Count valid routes in NPU DeepEP, including low-latency mode

DeepEP's communication mode and EPLB's statistics source are separate choices. This PR changes the statistics source; `low_latency` still uses low-latency dispatch, and `auto` still selects its communication mode at runtime.

In the existing gatherer factory, DeepEP `normal` uses TopK IDs, while `low_latency` uses receive-side expert counts. On NPU, graph-padding rows retain expert IDs for dispatch and have zero routing weights. Their receive counts therefore include rows that do not represent valid token routes. The NPU TopK path already provides a separate recorder view with those padded IDs masked to `-1`.

The factory now selects the existing TopK gatherer for NPU DeepEP in `normal`, `low_latency`, and `auto` modes. That gatherer counts the valid physical expert IDs and ignores `-1`; the shared accumulator reduces them and maps them to logical expert loads for the planner. No new recorder or counting kernel is introduced. Earlier `per_token` and `stat_approx` branches keep their existing selection rules, and GPU gatherer selection is unchanged.

For example, a graph bucket can contain eight rows with only four valid tokens. Zeroing the other four rows' routing weights does not remove their IDs from dispatch receive counts; masking those IDs in the recorder view excludes them from EPLB statistics. In the controlled two-rank check, real routes target rank 0 and padded routes target rank 1. Receive totals are `64/64`, while valid-route totals are `64/0`: the former reports balanced traffic even though the valid routes are entirely on rank 0.

## 2. Migrate NPU weights through ND storage

The common updater has one NPU dispatch branch. The NPU helper selects the changed layers and each rank's participation, validates TP = EP = WORLD and the selected chunk's tensor specifications, then calls the existing shared single-layer migration function.

For each participating layer:

1. Convert internal-format weights, such as NZ, to contiguous ND tensors; pack strided weights as needed. Contiguous ND weights are used directly.
2. Run the shared local-reordering and P2P algorithm on those tensors.
3. For changed local slots, restore the original format and copy into the original weight storage. This preserves addresses referenced by captured graphs.

A rank whose own slots are unchanged may still need to send an expert to another rank. It participates in that transfer but skips local writeback. With elastic EP enabled, the existing participation and missing-expert handling remain active.

Utilization-broadcast tensors also use the runtime device instead of hard-coded CUDA.

## 3. Control migration memory

These controls are included in this PR:

| Code behavior | Memory effect |
| --- | --- |
| Allocate receive buffers on the first participating layer and reuse them across the chunk | Avoid a separate receive-buffer set for every layer; idle ranks allocate none |
| Use the ND conversion result directly; reuse already-contiguous ND weights | Avoid an extra staging copy of those weights |
| Release each layer's ND references and use completion events to bound queued staging | Prevent the host from queuing temporary tensors for every layer while the device is still processing earlier transfers |
| Skip globally unchanged layers and ranks with no local changes or possible sends outside elastic EP | Avoid their conversion and receive-buffer allocations |
| Skip writeback when local slots are unchanged | Avoid unnecessary format-restoration tensors and copies on sender-only ranks |

The event queue retains two completion events; it waits before allocating further layer staging. Dropping Python references alone cannot bound the peak while earlier device work still uses that storage. The events allow completed storage to be reused by the allocator; cached memory can remain visible in device memory usage.

This controls migration's temporary allocations. Communication still uses default WORLD in this PR. TP-group reuse and draft-statistics isolation are in #47595, so their communication-memory savings are separate from these staging controls.

## Validation

- **16-rank Ascend HCCL:** five-layer migration with ND, NZ, and strided auxiliary weights; all ranks pass exact-value and original-storage-address checks using default WORLD. Tested source `f5f46fb1` has the same complete Git tree as initial PR commit [`950433a6`](https://github.com/AkiYangDev/sglang/commit/950433a6fdb7c378c132f6cf38fba95d47e3f30e). [Configuration, source checksums, and all rank results](https://github.com/AkiYangDev/sglang/blob/b091064f791ab77afd47b9ffb2e8f49b58dd4c67/eplb-micro-20261031/hccl_migration.json).
- **Two-rank Ascend DeepEP at [`950433a6`](https://github.com/AkiYangDev/sglang/commit/950433a6fdb7c378c132f6cf38fba95d47e3f30e):** production TopK counting captured and replayed in an NPU graph, with real eager low-latency dispatch/combine. With 8 allocated rows per rank, valid rows of `8/4/0/2` produce global TopK totals of `128/64/0/32`; receive totals remain `128`. Both ranks pass exact combine-output checks in balanced and controlled-skew cases. [Package versions, configuration, and per-expert counts](https://github.com/AkiYangDev/sglang/blob/b091064f791ab77afd47b9ffb2e8f49b58dd4c67/eplb-micro-20261031/deepep_counts.json).
- **CPU control-flow checks:** 400 migration configurations and 24 staging/buffer-lifetime cases pass after the readability update. Topology rejection occurs before staging initialization, and an empty update remains a no-op. The unchanged factory previously passed 144 selection comparisons, including 72 GPU cases matching main. Ruff, isort, syntax, and whitespace checks pass.

### GSM8K accuracy

Full GSM8K evaluation at [`2baffe85`](https://github.com/AkiYangDev/sglang/commit/2baffe85ad96b54c45fb0b3cfca0969c87c82b83), using `sgl-eval 0.1.3` on Ascend 910C:

| Metric | EPLB OFF | EPLB ON |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Correct / total | 1,285 / 1,319 | 1,285 / 1,319 |
| Accuracy | 97.42% | 97.42% |
| Request errors | 0 | 0 |
| Truncated responses | 0 | 0 |
| Completed rebalances per rank | 0 | 3 |
| Evaluation time | 376.355 s | 398.134 s |

All 1,319 final answers match. All 16 ranks complete three rebalances, and the installed expert layouts match the planner's targets. Of the evaluated questions, 910 start after the first update and 124 start after the third; their answers match OFF.

Both runs use DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8, single-node TP16/EP16/attention-DP16, DSpark gamma 5/verify 6, 16 redundant experts, and concurrency 16. Sampling uses temperature 0, top-p 1, seed 0, thinking disabled, and a 4,096-token output limit. KV capacity is 131,072 tokens, context length is 8,192, static memory fraction is 0.7, and radix cache is disabled. ON uses update interval 1,000 and statistics window 1,000. Both runs start from the same expert layout and complete two warm-up rounds; only `--enable-eplb` differs in the launch arguments.

[Evaluation configuration and all per-question results](https://github.com/AkiYangDev/sglang/blob/91e56e8ada29d7af82ae55c949726f6ffe5492ed/eplb-gsm8k-20261031/public_results.json)


### PD serving performance — 2026-10-29

Measured at [`f6ad2f4f`](https://github.com/AkiYangDev/sglang/commit/f6ad2f4f922d0df111dc66153f543a453267455c), the combined implementation with NPU integration, TP communication reuse, and draft-statistics isolation. The latter two changes are now split into #47595; the results below belong to that combined version.

| Setting | Both runs |
| --- | --- |
| Model / hardware | DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 W8A8; Ascend 910C, 8 cards / 16 NPU chips each for prefill and decode |
| Parallelism / speculation | TP16 / EP16 / attention-DP16 per side; DSpark gamma 5 / verify 6 |
| Experts / KV capacity | 16 redundant experts per side, identical trivial initial placement; P 369,024 / D 524,288 KV tokens |
| Workload | Synthetic long-text copying; 16,388 input / 12,288 output tokens; 1,536 requests, concurrency 256, no rate cap |
| Sampling / warmup | Temperature 0, ignore EOS, prefix cache disabled; 512 same-length warmup requests per run |
| ON update interval / window | P 50/50; D 4000/1000 |
| Runtime / client | CANN 9.1.0, torch-npu 2.10.0.post6, ais_bench 3.1.0; 1,800 s request timeout |

One OFF/ON pair, using ais_bench's native stable stage. Each stable window contains 1,280 requests at concurrency 256: 1,075.76 s for OFF and 1,027.27 s for ON. Rebalance costs are included.

| Native stable-stage metric | EPLB OFF | EPLB ON | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Output throughput, token/s | 14,620.99 | 15,311.06 | **+4.72%** |
| Mean TTFT, s | 15.80 | 13.45 | -14.89% |
| Mean TPOT, ms | 16.57 | 15.96 | -3.69% |
| Mean end-to-end latency, s | 219.46 | 209.59 | -4.49% |
| Mean ITL, ms | 95.68 | 92.09 | -3.75% |
| Successful / failed requests, full run | 1,536 / 0 | 1,536 / 0 | |
| Native acceptance-length gauge, mean | 5.7666 | 5.7512 | |
| Native acceptance-rate gauge, mean | 95.33% | 95.02% | |

Percentages use unrounded measurements. Acceptance gauges are rank/time sample means: AL ranges are 4.9266–6.0000 / 5.0047–6.0000 (OFF/ON), and acceptance-rate ranges are 78.53–100% / 80.09–100%. The actual proposed-token denominator was not recorded, so a global token-weighted acceptance rate is unavailable.

ON completed 11 prefill and 3 decode rebalances in the stable window. The native rebalance timer averaged 679.64 ms on P and 714.33 ms on D, taking the slowest rank per round.

<details>
<summary>P99 latency and original ais_bench terminal output</summary>

| P99 metric | EPLB OFF | EPLB ON |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| TTFT, s | 45.96 | 53.05 |
| TPOT, ms | 22.88 | 23.96 |
| End-to-end latency, s | 299.85 | 314.34 |
| ITL, ms | 192.72 | 184.05 |

P99 TTFT, TPOT, and end-to-end latency increased in this pair.

![EPLB OFF: original ais_bench stable-stage terminal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AkiYangDev/sglang/226d98f58db4402a79c8ce9b2ae8e6aabd9a0232/eplb-aisbench-20261029/OFF_native_result_retake.jpg)

+# limitations under the License.
+# ==============================================================================
+
+"""Ascend expert-weight staging and migration for EPLB.
+
+Callers select these helpers after NPU distributed initialization.
+Import torch_npu only when an NPU operation actually needs it.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections import deque
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Callable
+
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from sglang.srt.eplb.expert_location import ExpertLocationMetadata
+
+
+def update_expert_weights_with_staging(
+    weights_by_layer: dict[int, list[torch.Tensor]],
+    old_metadata: ExpertLocationMetadata,
+    new_metadata: ExpertLocationMetadata,
+    layer_ids: list[int],
+    nnodes: int,
+    rank: int,
+    log_metrics: bool,
+    update_layer_fn: Callable[..., None],
+) -> dict[int, list[int]]:
+    """Migrate each participating layer through ND storage, preserving model addresses."""
+    changed_layer_ids, local_update_plan = _select_expert_weight_updates(
+        old_metadata, new_metadata, layer_ids, rank
+    )
+    if not changed_layer_ids:
+        return {}
+
+    _validate_migration_topology()
+    staging = _ExpertWeightStaging(weights_by_layer, changed_layer_ids, rank)
+    world_size = dist.get_world_size()
+    temp_buffers = []
+    missing_experts_by_layer = {}
+
+    for layer, old_placement, new_placement, local_changed in local_update_plan:
+        weights = weights_by_layer[layer]
+        if not temp_buffers:
+            temp_buffers = staging.create_temp_buffers(weights)
+        migration_weights = staging.load(weights)
+        missing_experts = []
+        update_layer_fn(
+            routed_experts_weights=migration_weights,
+            temp_buffers=temp_buffers,
+            old_physical_to_logical_map=old_placement,
+            new_physical_to_logical_map=new_placement,
+            num_local_physical_experts=old_metadata.num_local_physical_experts,
+            num_gpu_per_node=world_size // nnodes,
+            rank=rank,
+            world_size=world_size,
+            missing_logical_experts_info=missing_experts,
+            log_metrics=log_metrics,
+        )
+        # Unchanged local slots may still send, but need no writeback.
+        if local_changed:
+            staging.store(weights, migration_weights)
+        # Release this layer's ND references before preparing the next layer.
+        del migration_weights
+        if missing_experts:
+            missing_experts_by_layer[layer] = missing_experts
+    return missing_experts_by_layer
+
+
+def _validate_migration_topology() -> None:
+    from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_parallel
+
+    parallel = get_parallel()
+    if (
+        parallel.tp_size != parallel.moe_ep_size
+        or parallel.moe_ep_size != dist.get_world_size()
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("NPU EPLB migration requires TP size = EP size = WORLD size.")
+
+
+def _select_expert_weight_updates(old_metadata, new_metadata, layer_ids, rank):
+    """Select globally updated layers and this rank's participating layers."""
+    from sglang.srt.elastic_ep.elastic_ep import ElasticEPStateManager
+
+    old_placements = old_metadata.physical_to_logical_map_cpu
+    new_placements = new_metadata.physical_to_logical_map_cpu
+    elastic_ep_enabled = ElasticEPStateManager.instance() is not None
+    changed_layer_ids = layer_ids
+    if not elastic_ep_enabled:
+        changed_layer_ids = [
+            layer
+            for layer in layer_ids
+            if not torch.equal(old_placements[layer], new_placements[layer])
+        ]
+    num_local_experts = old_metadata.num_local_physical_experts
+    start = rank * num_local_experts
+    local_slots = slice(start, start + num_local_experts)
+    local_update_plan = []
+    for layer in changed_layer_ids:
+        old_placement = old_placements[layer].tolist()
+        new_placement = new_placements[layer].tolist()
+        local_changed = old_placement[local_slots] != new_placement[local_slots]
+        if (
+            not elastic_ep_enabled
+            and not local_changed
+            and not _rank_may_send_experts(old_placement, new_placement, local_slots)
+        ):
+            continue
+        local_update_plan.append((layer, old_placement, new_placement, local_changed))
+    # Validate the whole selected chunk, including layers this rank skips.
+    return changed_layer_ids, local_update_plan
+
+
+def _rank_may_send_experts(old_placement, new_placement, local_slots):
+    """A possible sender holds an expert needed by a changed destination slot."""
+    local_experts = set(old_placement[local_slots])
+    return any(
+        old != new and new in local_experts
+        for old, new in zip(old_placement, new_placement, strict=True)
+    )
+
+
+def _validate_migration_weights(
+    weights_by_layer: dict[int, list[torch.Tensor]], layer_ids: list[int], rank: int
+) -> list[bool]:
+    """Validate chunk compatibility and return its ND staging requirements."""
+    import torch_npu
+
+    def specification(weights):
+        return [
+            (
+                tuple(t.shape),
+                t.dtype,
+                t.device,
+                torch_npu.get_npu_format(t) not in (0, 2) or not t.is_contiguous(),
+            )
+            for t in weights
+        ]
+
+    sample_layer = layer_ids[0]
+    expected = specification(weights_by_layer[sample_layer])
+    if not expected:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"[NPU EPLB] rank={rank} layer={sample_layer}: no expert weights"
+        )
+    for layer in layer_ids[1:]:
+        if specification(weights_by_layer[layer]) != expected:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"[NPU EPLB] rank={rank} layer={layer}: migration weights must match "
+                f"layer {sample_layer} in tensor count, shape, dtype, device, "
+                "and ND staging requirements"
+            )
+    return [needs_staging for _, _, _, needs_staging in expected]
+
+
+class _ExpertWeightStaging:
+    """Validate a chunk and prepare its weights for ND migration.
+
+    load() prepares the tensors that the updater mutates; store() copies the
+    result into model storage without changing addresses held by captured graphs.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        weights_by_layer: dict[int, list[torch.Tensor]],
+        layer_ids: list[int],
+        rank: int,
+    ):
+        # Convert internal formats and pack strided ND before migrating slices.
+        self._needs_staging = _validate_migration_weights(
+            weights_by_layer, layer_ids, rank
+        )
+        self._completion_events = deque(maxlen=2)
+
+    def create_temp_buffers(self, weights: list[torch.Tensor]) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+        return [
+            torch.empty(weight.shape, dtype=weight.dtype, device=weight.device)
+            for weight in weights
+        ]
+
+    def load(self, weights: list[torch.Tensor]) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+        # Bound queued work before allocating this layer's ND tensors.
+        # Each event follows the preceding layer's P2P waits and writeback.
+        # With two saved events, the fourth load waits for the first layer.
+        # The allocator can then reuse that layer's released ND storage.
+        if len(self._completion_events) == self._completion_events.maxlen:
+            self._completion_events.popleft().synchronize()
+        previous_layer_done = torch.npu.Event()
+        previous_layer_done.record()
+        self._completion_events.append(previous_layer_done)
+        # Keep the conversion result; copy_ would add another ND-to-ND copy.
+        return [
+            torch.ops.npu.npu_format_cast(weight, 2).contiguous() if needed else weight
+            for weight, needed in zip(weights, self._needs_staging)
+        ]
+
+    def store(
+        self, weights: list[torch.Tensor], migration_weights: list[torch.Tensor]
+    ) -> None:
+        for weight, buffer, needed in zip(
+            weights, migration_weights, self._needs_staging
+        ):
+            if not needed:
+                continue
+            restored = torch.ops.npu.npu_format_cast(
+                buffer, torch.ops.npu.get_npu_format(weight)
+            )
+            # Keep the storage addresses referenced by captured graphs.
+            weight.copy_(restored)
